articles.title: Illegal immigrant groping case latest allegation of misconduct in Northern Virginia school system
articles.summary: The Fairfax High groping case is the latest in a string of sexual misconduct cases that have put Fairfax County Public Schools under scrutiny in recent years.
articles.body: Virginia’s largest public school district is facing renewed scrutiny after parents accused Fairfax County Public Schools officials this week of delaying notification that an adult student identified as an illegal immigrant allegedly groped multiple female classmates. News broke last week that Israel Flores Ortiz, 19, a junior at Fairfax High School, was charged with nine counts of assault and battery after multiple female students accused him of inappropriately touching them while they were walking in school hallways between classes. Furious parents who spoke with Fox News Digital and local news outlet WJLA this week claim school officials waited two weeks to inform parents and the move only came after parental pressure. They also claim district officials sanitized the nature of the groping. The district said in a statement, "While Fairfax County Public Schools (FCPS) is unable to comment on specifics due to federal and state privacy laws, we prioritize student and staff safety and fully investigate any time someone reports an incident or says they do not feel safe at school. We are grateful to our law enforcement partners, who continue to work swiftly and thoroughly when there are safety concerns in our schools. The safety of all FCPS students and staff remains a top priority." SCHOOL BOARD SETTLES WITH BOYS ACCUSED OF SEXUAL HARASSMENT OVER TRANSGENDER STUDENT LOCKER ROOM INCIDENT The Fairfax High allegations follow several other criminal cases involving alleged sexual misconduct tied to FCPS schools in recent years. In September 2025, Thomas Edison High School instructional assistant Derrick Burroughs was arrested after Fairfax County police alleged he sexually assaulted two students on separate occasions. He was charged with two counts of aggravated sexual battery and indecent liberties by a custodian and put on administrative leave, according to police. The incident followed two other teachers in the district being arrested on sex crime charges in February 2025. Fairview Elementary School teacher John Barger was arrested and charged with two counts of aggravated sexual battery after detectives alleged he sexually assaulted two students on separate occasions. Later court reporting identified the students as ages 10 and 11. TRUMP ADMIN ASKS SPANBERGER, VIRGINIA OFFICIALS TO NOT RELEASE ILLEGAL CHARGED WITH GROPING HIGH SCHOOL GIRLS WJLA reported that parents questioned why they were not notified until weeks after the allegations surfaced. "We expect that anyone who works with children is focused on their safety and well-being," an FCPS spokesperson told WJLA 7News at the time. "When that trust is broken, it deeply affects us all. As soon as we were made aware of these allegations, the teacher was removed from our schools and has not returned." Also in February 2025, Falls Church High School teacher Richard Joseph Berkowitz was arrested in a Fairfax County child exploitation sting and charged with four counts of solicitation of a minor and two counts of production of child sexual abuse material, police said. Public reporting did not identify FCPS students as alleged victims in that case. He was suspended from teaching upon the arrest, according to authorities. In 2024, several other cases drew public attention. In September 2024, police charged former after-school contractor Arturo Elmore-Adon with seven counts of unlawful filming after investigators said they found videos he allegedly took of four girls, all FCPS elementary school students. VIRGINIA PROSECUTOR’S RECORD ON VIOLENT OFFENDERS SCRUTINIZED AFTER ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT CHARGED IN MOM'S MURDER At Langley High School, football coach and teacher David Clay Murray was arrested in August 2024 and charged with five counts of sexual solicitation of a minor, WJLA reported, after investigators said he solicited sex acts while communicating with an undercover detective posing as a 15-year-old girl. Then in October 2024, Langley instructional assistant David Scalea was arrested after police said a student reported seeing him masturbating in a classroom. He was charged with obscene sexual display and contributing to the delinquency of a minor, according to Fox5DC. In October 2023, Groveton Elementary School teacher James William Nugent II was charged with taking indecent liberties with a child and 13 counts of distributing child pornography after police said he exposed himself to a juvenile and investigators found child sexual abuse material during a search of his home. Police said they believed he may have exposed himself to other children in the area as well. In April 2023, James Madison High School learning disabilities teacher Allieh Kheradmand was charged with four counts of indecent liberties by a custodian after a student disclosed an inappropriate sexual relationship with her, according to the FCPD. articles.title: University leader admits schools are 'not a political party' in warning to elite campuses
articles.summary: Vanderbilt chancellor warns elite universities risk failure by prioritizing political activism over education mission amid Trump administration scrutiny.
articles.body: Vanderbilt University Chancellor Daniel Diermeier warned this week that America’s elite universities are in trouble if they continue to prioritize political activism over their mission of spreading knowledge. Diermeier joined the Washington Post’s "Reasonably Optimistic" podcast Wednesday to discuss the future of higher education and its role in culture wars. He stated that universities have become increasingly politicized, blaming that "mission drift" for the decrease of public trust in those institutions.   "The fundamental purpose of university is to be a place where you have path-breaking research and a transformative education." "The fundamental purpose of university is to be a place where you have path-breaking research and a transformative education," Diermeier said.  "You’re not a political party, and you're not part of a political movement," he added.  WHY ELITE COLLEGES FEAR TRUMP AND MCMAHON'S NEW ACADEMIC COMPACT TYING FUNDING TO FREE SPEECH Diermeier specifically blasted the use of "political litmus tests" in hiring faculty and staff at top schools.  He also criticized sorting incoming students into identity categories during orientation, saying it can lead to students being "socially ostracized" for challenging conventional wisdom. "When departments can't hire people or refuse to hire people based on their scholarly accomplishments, but when there's a political litmus test, you need to take action as a dean or president," Diermeier said. UNIVERSITY OF ALABAMA STUDENT JAMES GRACEY DISAPPEARS IN BARCELONA AFTER VISITING FRIENDS STUDYING ABROAD He argued it’s not all faculty on campuses stoking political fires, but often a "small but well-motivated and organized minority." Diermeier noted that many faculty members want to work rather than engage in political battles. "Once you enter the political battle, you're in the political battle, and that's where we are right now," he warned. In recent years, universities have been at the center of cultural controversies, including protests over the Israel-Hamas war and the Black Lives Matter movement.  In March 2024, several students were arrested or suspended for their actions during a protest at Vanderbilt over the war in Gaza. A House Committee on Education and the Workforce released a report Tuesday, which found some higher education faculty members "amplifying antisemitism." Last year, the Trump administration’s Department of Education announced that at least 60 universities were under investigation for antisemitism and harassment, including Ivy League schools.

articles.title: Sammy 'The Bull' Gravano recalls chilling mob request that helped clear John Gotti's path to power
articles.summary: Sammy Gravano reveals the shocking moment Angelo Ruggiero asked him to help John Gotti kill Gambino crime family boss Paul Castellano.
articles.body: Former Gambino crime family underboss Sammy "The Bull" Gravano dished on the moment he was asked to help pull off one of the mob's most audacious power plays — the murder of John Gotti's own boss. "We have problems with Paul. I need your help. We need you — me and John Gotti," Gravano recalled being told by Gotti associate Angelo Ruggiero. "I said, 'To do what?'" he recounted on the "Hang Out With Sean Hannity" podcast. SAMMY 'THE BULL' REVEALS WHY HIS LOVE FOR JOHN GOTTI TURNED INTO PRISON HATE "We're gonna kill him." The target was Paul Castellano, then-boss of the Gambino crime family, one of the most powerful figures in organized crime — making the request anything but an ordinary mob "favor." "You're gonna kill the boss of bosses?" Gravano recalled asking, prompting Ruggiero to respond, "Yes, and we need your help." The gravity of the request wasn't lost on him, he told host Sean Hannity. A hit on a boss could carry serious — even deadly — consequences for everyone involved. Gravano recalled pressing the issue and asking where Gotti was himself. JOHN GOTTI PAL: I STASHED $10M IN MY KID'S TOYCHEST "I told him, 'Angelo, first of all, where's John Gotti? You're talking to me. Where is he?'" The back-and-forth between the two men continued, with Ruggiero insisting that Gotti "had something to do." "[I said], 'He had something more important than asking me to kill the boss of bosses or help you kill the boss of bosses? I don't know what's more important than that,'" Gravano recounted. "This is a big deal," he added. Castellano and his new underboss, Thomas Bilotti, were ultimately murdered outside a New York City steakhouse in 1985. Gotti was the mastermind behind the incident and would soon be convicted for ordering the crime. Gravano's sit-down conversation with Hannity went beyond the incident, into his time with the mob, his involvement in nearly 20 murders and much more. articles.title: American Federation of Teachers launches boycott against Target, claims retailer 'remained silent' on ICE
articles.summary: Randi Weingarten launched an AFT back-to-school boycott of Target over ICE silence, but critics say pension fund leverage warrants a federal probe.
articles.body: American Federation of Teachers (AFT) President Randi Weingarten promoted a nationwide back-to-school boycott of retail giant Target over the weekend because the company had not condemned ICE operations in Minnesota — the location of its headquarters — prompting criticism from education advocates and a call for federal scrutiny. "We gave Target ample time to stand with the communities in which they operate and help their neighbors, but its silence about federal immigration abuses has been deafening," Weingarten said in a statement. "The issue could not be more pressing: Seven months since the murders of Alex Pretti and Renée Good, masked ICE agents are still in our streets, our schools and our communities, terrorizing families in the name of Donald Trump’s illegal and immoral assault on immigrants striving for their American Dream," she continued. "That’s why we’re urging our members to avoid Target and patronize more ethical shopping alternatives this back-to-school season." Weingarten also shared a video on Instagram, where she directed families to the AFT’s "Shop Smart, Not Target" website, which maps local back-to-school shopping alternatives. The organization launched the campaign Wednesday after sending Target CEO Michael Fiddelke letters in February and March. WATCH: WEINGARTEN GESTURES WILDLY DURING ANTI-TRUMP RANT, LATER SAYS HE DRIVES HER TO DRINK Corey DeAngelis, a Heritage Foundation research fellow, told Fox News Digital Sunday that using the organization’s pension influence against Target raised fiduciary concerns and warranted a federal investigation. "This partisan war on Target smells like a breach of fiduciary duty given that AFT members’ pension funds own 6.79 million shares of Target stock, which Weingarten has already leveraged to pressure the company into opposing ICE," he said. "The Department of Justice should open an investigation into the AFT using their pension funds and political influence to bully companies into falling in line with their socialist agenda." "Urging educators and families to avoid Target is not an appropriate use of the union’s resources or influence," he added.  This isn't the AFT's first time batting against the retail giant. DeAngelis also supplied Fox News Digital with a chart tracking Target’s closing share price against several AFT actions, including Weingarten’s letters and the organization’s March boycott resolution. TEACHERS UNION FACING YEARS OF DEFICITS SEEKS TO BECOME OREGON'S LARGEST PAC, INTERNAL DOCUMENTS SHOW Sonja Shaw, a candidate for California superintendent of public instruction and Chino Valley Unified School District board president, told Fox News Digital on Sunday that labor leaders were prioritizing political power while students continued to struggle academically. "Teachers’ unions are supposed to fight for teachers. Instead, union leadership has become a political machine obsessed with money, power and influence while our children continue to fall behind," she said. "In California, more than half our students are not proficient in basic reading and math. When a system produces those results year after year, that isn’t success. That’s education malpractice." California's latest statewide assessments showed 48.8% of students met or exceeded English language arts standards and 37.3% met or exceeded math standards. The AFT's March resolution explicitly called the effort a boycott and urged its 1.8 million members, families and allies to avoid Target until the company stood with the Twin Cities. TEXAS’ LARGEST SCHOOL DISTRICT SEES TEST SCORES SOAR AFTER STATE TAKEOVER DESPITE RACISM CLAIMS DeAngelis’ request followed Sen. Eric Schmitt’s, R-Missouri, July appeal for the Labor Department to investigate whether AFT leaders coordinated with retirement-plan fiduciaries to use members’ assets for political objectives. House lawmakers separately demanded answers about reports that member dues helped finance Weingarten’s book, "Why Fascists Fear Teachers," while she received royalties. Teachers spend an average of $895 of their own money every year on supplies their students need, according to a 2025 teacher spending survey. articles.title: Ten Commandments belong in Texas schools and the Supreme Court can protect them
articles.summary: The U.S. Supreme Court faces a pivotal decision on whether Texas public schools can constitutionally display the Ten Commandments in classrooms.
articles.body: The U.S. Supreme Court has been asked to decide if the Ten Commandments can be posted in Texas public schools. In the coming months, the justices will decide whether or not to review a decision by the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Fifth Circuit which found that the posting the Ten Commandments in schools is not only constitutional, but also consistent with America’s historical understanding of religion’s role in public life. Documents and history are not banned in this country because they are religious or have religious content. Are students allowed to read the Rev. Martin Luther King Jr.’s "Letter from Birmingham Jail?" Of course they are. TEXAS BOARD OF EDUCATION APPROVES REQUIRED READING LIST WITH BIBLE PASSAGES FOR 5 MILLION STUDENTS Banning parts of our religious history and heritage is not an act of compliance with the First Amendment. It is hostility to religion and a religious cleansing, foreign to our Constitution. The First Amendment forbids the government from establishing an official state religion — something akin to the Church of England, where the state controlled doctrine, compelled worship and punished dissenters. The Fifth Circuit’s ruling made clear that such "establishments" historically involved acts of coercion such as mandatory church attendance or legal penalties for noncompliance. Displaying a religious text on a classroom wall bears no resemblance to such practices. SUPREME COURT SHOWDOWN LOOMS OVER ST MICHAEL STATUE BLOCKED FROM PUBLIC SAFETY BUILDING The Ten Commandments are a foundational moral, literary and historical text. Their influence on Western legal traditions is widely acknowledged, even by critics. The Commandments articulate basic ethical principles such as prohibitions against murder, theft and perjury that underpin modern legal systems. Displaying them in classrooms is simply a recognition of their historical and cultural significance. A quality education must include instruction on the religious and historical heritage of our country. Without it, students cannot understand the founding rationale of our nation, nor its system of laws. JUDGE ORDERS WASHINGTON SCHOOL DISTRICT TO LOOSEN LIMITS ON OFF-CAMPUS BIBLE CLUB FOR PUBLIC SCHOOL STUDENTS Critics argue that posting the Ten Commandments amounts to coercion, especially for impressionable students. But this claim does not withstand scrutiny. The Texas law at issue requires only that a poster be displayed. It does not mandate prayer, belief or participation in any religious activity. Students are not asked to recite the Commandments, affirm their truth or even engage with them at all. In other words, exposure is not indoctrination. This distinction is crucial. Public education inevitably exposes students to a wide range of historical, philosophical, and, yes, religious ideas. The Constitution does not demand that schools become religion-free zones; rather, it protects against government coercion in matters of faith. As the Fifth Circuit notes, "the mere presence of religious language in a school display is [not] ipso facto religious coercion." If it were, many longstanding features of American public life, from the national motto "In God We Trust" to references to a "Creator" in the Declaration of Independence, would be constitutionally suspect. GOP LAWMAKERS URGE SUPREME COURT TO STRENGTHEN FIRST AMENDMENT PROTECTIONS FOR STREET PREACHERS The legal foundation for the Fifth Circuit’s conclusion rests heavily on First Liberty Institute’s victory in Kennedy v. Bremerton School District, which fundamentally reshaped Establishment Clause jurisprudence. As the Fifth Circuit explains, Kennedy abandoned the long-criticized "Lemon test" and replaced it with an approach rooted in "historical practices and understandings." Under this framework, courts no longer ask whether a government action has a secular purpose, but whether it resembles the kinds of coercive religious establishments the Founders sought to prohibit. This shift is decisive: because a classroom display imposes no religious exercise, no punishment for dissent and no government control over belief, it falls far outside the historical definition of an "establishment of religion." In short, Kennedy clarifies that the Constitution protects against coercion, not mere exposure to religious ideas, history and heritage. RARE AMERICAN BIBLE AND FOUNDERS’ LETTERS TRACE FAITH’S ROLE IN BIRTH OF THE NATION The Founders themselves did not envision a strict separation of religion from public education. As Judge James Ho quoted President George Washington in his concurrence, they believed that "religion and morality are indispensable supports" of a free society. Far from excluding religion, early American institutions often incorporated it as a source of moral guidance and civic virtue. Public education inevitably exposes students to a wide range of historical, philosophical, and, yes, religious ideas. The Constitution does not demand that schools become religion-free zones; rather, it protects against government coercion in matters of faith. Just consider the U.S. Supreme Court building where the Ten Commandments are displayed both on the outer façade of the courthouse as well as the internal courtroom itself. Do the justices need to sandblast those images from the court? Removing all the references to the Biblical Decalogue built into the architecture of government buildings throughout Washington, D.C., would require jackhammers, chisels and high-powered sand blasters. CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION Allowing such displays respects both the Constitution and the nation’s heritage. It’s also good education. It acknowledges the role that religious ideas have played in shaping American law and culture, without compelling anyone to adopt those beliefs. In a pluralistic society, exposure to diverse perspectives, including religious ones, is not a threat to freedom, it is a reflection of it. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Rather than fearing the presence of the Ten Commandments in classrooms, the plaintiffs should recognize it for what it is: a modest, constitutionally sound acknowledgment of the moral and historical foundations that continue to influence our society today. articles.title: Houston Uber driver caught in wild police chase as officers seen on dashcam video hitching a ride in his car
articles.summary: The dashcam video shows Houston police riding with the Uber driver for several minutes before spotting the suspect and resuming pursuit on foot.
articles.body: A Houston Uber driver was caught "off guard" but kept his cool when two police officers jumped into his vehicle and directed him to chase a suspect fleeing on foot, frantic dashcam video shows. Anthony Baines said he was driving for Uber at about 12:20 a.m. Aug. 8 in a Houston Heights neighborhood, when a shirtless man ran across the street in front of his vehicle with two Houston Police Department officers close behind, according to Storyful. The video shows Baines getting waved down by an officer and stopping as she approaches and hops into the front passenger seat. HANDCUFFED SUSPECT ALLEGEDLY SLIPS RESTRAINTS, STEALS DALLAS POLICE CRUISER WITH OFFICER TRAPPED IN BACK SEAT "Hey, give me a ride over there please," the officer says in the video. "Go, go that way … go, go, go, go, go!" Baines can be heard asking which way he should drive as officers point him in the direction of the suspect. After driving a short distance, the officer signals for her partner, who's carrying a flashlight, to get in the vehicle, too, and opens the car door and jumps into the backseat. RIDESHARE PASSENGER HELD HOSTAGE FOR EIGHT HOURS DURING ARMED STANDOFF WITH POLICE IN SWANKY NEIGHBORHOOD The officers rode with Baines for several minutes while searching the area before one of them appeared to spot the suspect. Both officers jump out of the Uber and resume their pursuit on foot. "What the f---?!" Baines is heard saying as the officers dart from his car. BODYCAM SHOWS POLICE K-9 LEAPING INTO ACTION AFTER SUSPECTED IMPAIRED DRIVER REFUSED TO SURRENDER "It caught me completely off guard," Baines told Storyful. "I’ve never had anything like that happen driving. I was surprised but just did what the officer asked in the moment." Houston police confirmed the authenticity of the video and the incident to KPRC 2, which reported officers had been responding to a terroristic threat call involving allegations that the suspect threatened to shoot a woman and her children after becoming upset over a belief that someone had stolen from him. Police said officers tried to detain the man as he left an apartment, but he refused to cooperate and ran away. An officer asked the driver to take them around the block to the apartment complex, where the officers returned to their own vehicle, according to KPRC. FLORIDA MAN ARRESTED IN IHOP RESTAURANT AFTER POLICE SAY HE STABBED A RIDESHARE DRIVER Despite the unusual assistance, police did not locate the suspect. His identity has not been released, and the investigation remains ongoing. Baines later appeared to confirm in a social media post that he was the Uber driver behind the dashcam footage. "Yep, that was me," he wrote. "The Uber driver whose dashcam caught two HPD officers jumping in my car to chase a suspect." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Baines described himself as an Army veteran, husband and father of two who began driving Uber so he and his wife could save for their first home. Fox News Digital has reached out to HPD and Uber for comment.

articles.summary: Drew Andres Owens was released from Mecklenburg County Jail just three days before CMS students returned to class after allegedly threatening five schools.
articles.body: A Charlotte man indicted on five felony counts accusing him of threatening mass shootings against five area public schools was released from jail just three days before students were scheduled to return to class. Drew Andres Owens, 33, was released from the Mecklenburg County Jail at 11:30 a.m. on Aug. 22, according to jail records. Charlotte-Mecklenburg Schools students were scheduled to return on Aug. 25. A Mecklenburg County grand jury indicted Owens in March 2025 on five counts of communicating threats of mass violence on educational property. He has pleaded not guilty, and the cases remain pending. THREE SCHOOL SAFETY STEPS EVERY PARENT SHOULD KNOW BEFORE CLASSES BEGIN Four counts allege Owens sent emails on Feb. 15, 2025, threatening West Charlotte High School, Ardrey Kell High School, Community House Middle School and Hawk Ridge Elementary School. According to court documents reviewed by Fox News Digital, Owens allegedly sent messages threatening to "slaughter staff and students." SUBSTITUTE TEACHER ARRESTED AFTER ALLEGEDLY TRIGGERING FALSE ACTIVE SHOOTER ALERTS AT 5 SCHOOLS: SHERIFF A separate indictment alleges a mailed threat against Garinger High School. The affidavit claimed that a student, who was armed with two shotguns and an AR-15, would carry out the mass shooting. School administrators later determined that no student by that name was enrolled there, according to the affidavit. The warrant affidavit states that Darryl Owens, Drew's father and a West Charlotte High School ROTC instructor, told police he also believed his son was responsible for the school threats. FOLLOW US ON X Darryl Owens allegedly told authorities that his son had harassed relatives, neighbors and family friends after being removed from the family home in 2021, and had sent unsigned emails and letters threatening to kill or shoot people at multiple locations. SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST TRUE CRIME NEWS The father told police he had previously obtained a restraining order against his son, that Owens had been arrested for violating it and that the order was later dismissed. He also told police that Owens had recently sat outside neighbors' homes and photographed his car at West Charlotte High School "to try to lure him outside." Docket records indicate the four-school case had originally been set at a $135,000 secured bond with electronic monitoring in February 2025. GET BREAKING NEWS ALERTS A judge reduced that amount to $60,000 on May 1, 2026. The separate case tied to Garinger High School carried a secured bond of $15,000. Owens satisfied the court-ordered pretrial bond conditions and was released Saturday, Aug. 22. A professional surety posted the $60,000 bond the previous Friday night. GOT A TIP? articles.title: Muere una niña de ocho años infectada por la parásito 'comecerebros': pudo contagiarse mientras se bañaba en un lago
articles.standfirst: El hecho se produjo en Louisiana
articles.summary: El hecho se produjo en Louisiana
articles.body: Una niña de ocho años ha fallecido en Louisiana (Estados Unidos) tras contraer una extraña infección causada por la ameba Naegleria fowleri, conocida popularmente como la "ameba comecerebros". Según las autoridades sanitarias, la menor pudo haberse contagiado del parásito microscópico mientras se bañaba en un lago cercano a su domicilio. La víctima, Lillian Smart, vecina de Ruston, moría en un hospital apenas un día después de celebrar su octavo cumpleaños. La noticia fue confirmada por su familia a través de una publicación en redes sociales, recogida posteriormente por medios como CNN y The Guardian. "Anoche Lillian pasó de nuestros brazos a los brazos de Jesús", escribió su familia. "Las lesiones en su cerebro eran demasiado graves para que su pequeño cuerpo pudiera recuperarse. Todos hicieron todo lo posible por salvarla. Estamos destrozados y no sabemos cómo seguir adelante", añadieron. El Departamento de Salud de Louisiana informó el pasado 19 de agosto de un caso de infección por Naegleria fowleri en un residente del estado, cuya exposición al organismo se habría producido durante un baño en el lago Claiborne, situado a unos 48 kilómetros al noroeste de Ruston. Aunque las autoridades no revelaron inicialmente la identidad de la paciente, familiares y allegados confirmaron después a medios locales que se trataba de Lillian. Se trata de un organismo microscópico que habita en aguas dulces cálidas, como lagos, ríos y estanques. La infección se produce cuando el agua contaminada entra por la nariz, permitiendo que la ameba alcance el cerebro. Una vez allí, puede provocar una meningoencefalitis amebiana primaria, una enfermedad extremadamente rara, pero con una tasa de mortalidad muy elevada. Aunque los casos son poco frecuentes, las autoridades sanitarias recuerdan que el riesgo aumenta durante los meses más cálidos y recomiendan extremar las precauciones en aguas dulces templadas o calientes, especialmente al bucear o realizar actividades que favorezcan la entrada de agua por las fosas nasales.

articles.title: Jury convicts Kevin Salazar in execution-style killing of LA Deputy Ryan Clinkunbroomer
articles.summary: Kevin Salazar was convicted of murdering Los Angeles County deputy Ryan Clinkunbroomer in a 2023 drive-by ambush near his Palmdale station.
articles.body: A California man has been convicted in the drive-by ambush of a Los Angeles deputy shot and killed at a red light just steps from the sheriff's Palmdale station in 2023. Jurors found Kevin Salazar, 32, guilty of the murder of Deputy Ryan Clinkunbroomer Monday after a week-long trial. "It’s very helpful that the justice system prevail, that you have a conviction that is a benefit to the family," Brad Gage, the Los Angeles attorney representing Clinkunbroomer's family, told Fox News Digital. "That gives some solace. That gives some comfort." MURDERED LOS ANGELES SHERIFF'S DEPUTY'S FAMILY SLAPS COUNTY WITH $20M WRONGFUL DEATH LAWSUIT Around 6 p.m. on Sept. 16, 2023, Clinkunbroomer pulled up to a red light down the street from the sheriff's station in Palmdale. He was driving his marked car and wearing his uniform. As he waited for the light to turn green, another car pulled up alongside him – and a man inside shot him in the head. Authorities said Salazar had followed Clinkunbroomer from the Palmdale Sheriff's Station to the intersection less than a block away before opening fire with a .22 revolver. He sped off, and Clinkunbroomer was pronounced dead at a hospital. Authorities found Salazar at his family's home in Palmdale two days later and arrested him on murder charges after a standoff, part of which was caught on video. ARREST MADE IN AMBUSH KILLING OF LA SHERIFF'S DEPUTY RYAN CLINKUNBROOMER Clinkunbroomer, 30, was engaged to be married at the time of his murder. "When a parent loses a child, there’s no name for it," Gage said. "It’s so painful, it’s so traumatic, it is so devastating that it is beyond words." Jurors deliberated for just 2 1/2 hours before finding Salazar guilty of first-degree murder as well as the special circumstance allegations of murder of a peace officer, lying in wait and firing from a vehicle, according to the Los Angeles County District Attorney's Office. WATCH: Suspect arrested following fatal shooting of LA sheriff’s deputy Ryan Clinkunbroomer Despite the conviction, a motive remains unclear, according to the family's attorney. "As far as we know, there was no reason," Gage told Fox News Digital. "It was just execution of a police officer." The court will move on Wednesday to a sanity-deciding phase for Salazar, to determine whether he goes to prison or is confined in a state mental hospital after he raised an insanity defense. SEND US A TIP "This brutal and senseless murder took the life of a dedicated deputy, leaving his family, colleagues and community to endure an unimaginable loss. We hope today’s guilty verdict brings a measure of healing to Deputy Clinkunbroomer’s family and loved ones," Los Angeles County District Attorney Nathan Hochman said in a statement. Clinkunbroomer came from a law enforcement family. His grandfather, father and brother all served. LISTEN TO THE NEW 'CRIME & JUSTICE WITH DONNA ROTUNNO' PODCAST "Ryan dedicated his life to service, proudly carrying on his family’s legacy as a third-generation member of the Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department," Sheriff Robert Luna said after the verdict. "We will forever honor his service, his sacrifice and the badge he proudly wore. Deputy Ryan Clinkunbroomer will never be forgotten." After his death, the family sued the county, alleging that mandatory overtime and understaffing had left Clinkunbroomer exhausted and more vulnerable to the ambush, Gage said. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP The county was dismissed from the lawsuit based on workers' compensation protections, however, and the family decided not to pursue a civil case against Salazar. Separately, the county honored Clinkunbroomer by renaming a Department of Parks and Recreation sports complex after him in January 2026.

articles.title: Incendio en Barcelona: 35 hectáreas de Collserola afectadas y dos barrios confinados
articles.standfirst: Los vecinos de Ciutat Meridiana y Torre Baró han recibido un mensaje de ES-Alert
articles.summary: Los vecinos de Ciutat Meridiana y Torre Baró han recibido un mensaje de ES-Alert
articles.body: Un incendio en el parque Collserola (Barcelona) originado alrededor de las 15:30 horas ha obligado a las autoridades a confinar los barrios de Ciutat Meridiana y Torre Baró, en los que viven unas 15.000 personas. "Se ordena el confinamiento de la población de los barrios de Torre Baró y Ciutat Meridiana debido al incendio de vegetación. Cierren puertas y ventanas, detengan los sistemas de ventilación y no salgan a la calle", puede leerse en el texto recibido. De forma preventiva, las autoridades también han desalojado a los vecinos de las calles Castellví y Lliçà del barrio de Torre Baró. Son las dos que están más cerca del incendio. Las autoridades han mandado dos mensajes ES-Alert. El primero, a las 16:45 horas, indicando el confinamiento. El segundo, a las 18:30, en el que se ha insistido en respetar las instrucciones de las autoridades y mantener el civismo en esta situación delicada. El humo se ha visto desde varias zonas de la ciudad y el teléfono de emergencias (112) ha recibido más de mil llamadas de aviso. El incendio afecta a un total de 35 hectáreas, según los datos provisionales ofrecidos por Agents Rurals. Por su parte, Bomberos de la Generalitat ha informado que un total de 160 efectivos y 60 dotaciones, doce aéreas, están trabajando activamente en la zona. Por el momento, las autoridades desconocen el origen del incendio. El fuego se ha iniciado en una zona de matorrales de la carretera alta de Roquetes, en el distrito de Nou Barris y avanza hacia Sant Cugat del Vallès y Cerdanyola del Vallès. Sergi Bové, jefe de intervención de Bomberos de Barcelona, ha atendido a los medios alrededor de las 19:30 horas: "Esperamos que la situación mejore ambientalmente en las próximas horas y podamos controlar los flancos, que es lo que nos preocupa. Lo que debemos de procurar es que no se produzca un cambio de condiciones peor por la noche, un cambio de viento, y que se descontrolen los dos flancos. No podemos dar ninguna previsión". El alcalde de Barcelona, Jaume Collboni, presente en la zona, ha agradecido el trabajo de bomberos y el resto de autoridades en el incendio. "Como alcalde, pido que se sigan los consejos de Protección Civil. Esperamos que en las próximas horas todo pueda estar controlado. articles.title: ICE lodges detainer for illegal immigrant with lengthy rap sheet after alleged jealousy-fueled killing
articles.summary: ON FOX: Federal immigration officials lodged an ice detainer for a Cuban citizen with drug trafficking convictions charged with second-degree murder.
articles.body: FIRST ON FOX: Federal immigration officials are asking authorities in the Miami area to honor a detainer request for an illegal immigrant with a lengthy criminal history who is now charged with fatally shooting a man on the street in an alleged act of jealousy. William Serrano Domenech, 49, is being held in a Miami-Dade County jail in connection with the Aug. 17 murder of 42-year-old Raul Aballe, the Department of Homeland Security said Tuesday. "He has a rap sheet a mile long, with prior convictions in Florida and Michigan for drug trafficking and illegal possession of a firearm, as well as prior arrests in New Mexico and Tennessee for aggravated assault, theft, and resisting arrest," Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said in a statement to Fox News Digital. "This dangerous criminal should have never been in our country, and had it not been for the Biden Administration releasing him from ICE custody in 2023, Raul Aballe would still be alive." EXCLUSIVE: DHS SEEKS CUSTODY OF ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT CHARGED WITH MURDER AFTER TRUMP DEPORTATION, BIDEN RELEASE Domenech, a Cuban citizen, was "socializing with the witness" on the evening of the slaying when Aballe appeared and the pair began arguing, authorities said. The dispute turned physical when Domenech started punching and slapping Aballe, authorities said. Domenech allegedly pulled a gun out of a fanny pack and opened fire, striking Aballe in the stomach. Aballe was taken to a hospital where he later died. ICE LODGES DETAINER ON SALVADORAN NATIONAL, 18, ACCUSED OF 2 FATAL SHOOTINGS IN HOUSTON Domenech allegedly fled the scene, but he was arrested the next day. He allegedly admitted to the killing and said he was jealous of Aballe's relationship with the witness, according to authorities. The witness reportedly told investigators that Aballe was not armed and didn't initiate the fight. HOW A NONCITIZEN SUSPECTED KILLER GOT CAUGHT AND RELEASED BY NEWSOM-APPOINTED JUDGE: TIMELINE Domenech is charged with second-degree murder and possession of a firearm by a convicted felon. U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) lodged a detainer with Miami-Dade authorities the day after Domenech's arrest. His criminal history spans at least four states for a litany of offenses, DHS said. That includes a conviction for a weapons offense and arrests on charges of vehicle theft, burglary, driving without a license, and driving with a suspended license in Florida, as well as prior arrests on charges of aggravated assault with a deadly weapon, false imprisonment, and bribery of a witness in New Mexico. HUNDREDS OF JAILED ILLEGAL ALIENS RELEASED BACK ONTO BLUE-STATE STREETS DESPITE ICE DETAINERS, RECORDS SHOW In addition, Domenech has prior arrests for unlawful possession of a weapon, resisting arrest, and theft in Tennessee, and convictions for possession with intent to distribute five grams or more of cocaine, possession with intent to distribute an unknown quantity of marijuana, possession of firearms in furtherance of a drug trafficking crime, possession of a firearm by an illegal alien, and felon in possession of a firearm in Michigan, authorities said. Domenech allegedly told authorities he entered the United States through Florida in 1995. A deportation order was issued by a judge in 2002. ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT CHARGED WITH BRUTAL SLAYING ONE DAY AFTER CALIFORNIA JUDGE RELEASED HIM: DHS However, when ICE took him into custody in 2023, he was released back onto the streets by the Biden administration, DHS said. articles.title: Mystery trio in headlamps and overalls emerges from Manhattan manhole, prompting NYPD probe
articles.summary: The NYPD is reviewing surveillance video after three people in overalls and headlamps were caught emerging from a Manhattan manhole near Penn Station.
articles.body: The New York Police Department is investigating after video showing three people in overalls and headlamps emerging from a Manhattan manhole went viral on social media. articles.title: Globetrotting sailor nabbed in Canada over alleged child sex crimes aboard sailboat: feds
articles.summary: Donald Steven Lang, 62, was arrested in Canada after the FBI warned the alleged child predator could be sailing across the Pacific to evade authorities.
articles.body: An alleged child predator accused of exploiting a child aboard his sailboat was arrested in Canada, after the FBI warned he could be sailing across the Pacific Ocean to evade authorities. Donald Steven Lang, 62, was taken into custody over the weekend at the request of the United States, federal authorities said Tuesday, ending a far-reaching search for the globe-trotting sailor. Lang, a dual U.S. and Canadian citizen, was indicted Aug. 20 in Hawaii on one count of sexual exploitation of children. 'AMERICA'S MOST WANTED' FUGITIVE CAPTURED ON SAILBOAT OFF NJ COAST AFTER 20 YEARS ON THE RUN Prosecutors allege he exploited a minor between September and December 2024 aboard his 55-foot sailboat, Ishi. The Department of Justice (DOJ) said Lang was known to sail around the world and frequently harbored in Hawaii. But the FBI’s search for him extended far beyond the islands. 'AMERICA'S MOST WANTED' FUGITIVE LAID BLUEPRINT FOR VANISHING BEFORE 20-YEAR ESCAPE: AFFIDAVIT The bureau warned Lang, who was last seen on board Ishi in Hawaii in January 2025, could have been sailing between Hawaii and Fiji or Mexico, headed toward Papua New Guinea, or possibly Indonesia. He had ties or connections in Hawaii, Idaho, Washington state, California, Fiji, the Marquesas Islands, Mexico and Canada, the FBI said. Federal prosecutors allege that Lang attempted to and knowingly used, persuaded, induced, enticed or coerced a minor to engage in sexually explicit conduct for the purpose of producing visual depictions. The indictment identifies his sailboat as a 55-foot, 1985 Taylor Hatfield oceangoing sailing vessel. Prosecutors are seeking forfeiture of the boat, digital devices and storage media, including a Samsung Galaxy S22 Ultra phone, should Lang be convicted. 'AMERICA'S MOST WANTED' EX-COP FUGITIVE RETURNED AFTER 20 YEARS ON THE RUN TO FACE MURDER, CHILD SEX CHARGES Lang was already wanted in Idaho in a separate child sex abuse case, authorities said. Kootenai County prosecutors charged Lang in April 2025 with three counts of lewd conduct towards a minor under 16 and one count of sexual battery of a minor in connection with allegations that he sexually assaulted a minor between 2003 and 2007. MORE THAN 300 ARRESTED IN SPRAWLING CALIFORNIA CRACKDOWN ON CHILD EXPLOITATION CRIMES "Protecting children from sexual predators is a priority of the highest order," Assistant Attorney General A. Tysen Duva said. "We will continue to pursue this alleged offender and work with our law enforcement partners to return him to the United States to face trial for the crimes he is charged with committing." FBI Criminal Assistant Director Heith Janke said Lang had been accused by multiple victims of sexually abusing minors. FBI ANNOUNCES 305 ARRESTS, 24 MISSING CHILDREN RECOVERED IN CHICAGO DURING OPERATION NEW DAWN "The FBI remains committed to identifying, investigating, and bringing offenders to justice who prey on some of the most vulnerable members of our communities," Janke said. The FBI had offered a reward of up to $5,000 for information leading to Lang’s arrest and warned he should be considered an escape risk. ALLEGED IRISH CARTEL BOSS ARRESTED IN COVERT OPERATION ON ORGANIZED CRIME CHARGES AFTER YEARS-LONG MANHUNT Lang’s apprehension came through cooperation between the FBI and the Royal Canadian Mounted Police’s Pacific Region, authorities said. The RCMP’s Tofinoofino General Duty, Island District GIS, Nanaimo Detachment and Island District ERT assisted in the arrest, while the Justice Department’s Office of International Affairs helped secure it. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP If convicted in the Hawaii case, Lang faces a mandatory minimum of 15 years in prison and up to 30 years behind bars. He could also face a fine of up to $250,000 and supervised release of between five years and life.

articles.title: California school district sued over field trip to mosque where students allegedly donned Muslim garb
articles.summary: Multi-faith parents sued Palo Alto High School claiming students were given hijabs and Qurans during a mosque field trip last year without parental consent.
articles.body: A group of multi-faith parents has filed a joint lawsuit against Palo Alto Unified School District in California and Palo Alto High School's principal Brent Kline over a field trip to a local mosque last year. According to the August 7 lawsuit, as part of the school's Social Justice Pathway curriculum, students took a tour of a mosque hosted by the Muslim Community Association and took part in several religious activities and were allegedly encouraged to don religious garb without parental consent. "During the Fall 2025 mosque visit, students who were minors allegedly were provided with Muslim religious attire and encouraged to wear it while on site," the complaint read. "During that visit, students allegedly were provided with Qurans and taught that Islam, in particular, promotes social justice." TEXAS TEEN TELLS CONGRESS HE RECEIVED DEATH THREATS AFTER REVEALING ISLAMIC BOOTH AT HIGH SCHOOL "The field-trip activities allegedly included observation of a Dhuhr prayer, discussion of the meaning of worship, and engagement with participants in the Noor Hifz Academy, the host institution’s religious youth program in which Islamic students memorize the Quran," the complaint continued. "Female students were provided hijabs to wear and that all students were gifted Qurans to take home for personal use." The lawsuit, which was filed by a group of Jewish, Hindu and Zoroastrian parents, also claimed that students spoke to Zahra Billoo, the executive director of the Bay Area office of the Council on American-Islamic Relations, who has come under controversy for making allegedly antisemitic statements in the past. In a comment to Fox News Digital, David Rosenberg-Wohl, who is representing the parents, said that the issue at hand is a public school like Palo Alto High School specifically promoting Islam in its Social Justice Pathway curriculum.  "In effect, kids are being told that if they are progressive and interested in social justice, Islam is the faith for them. That is not the business of a public school. It's not an issue of religion v. religion. It's an American one. The separation of church and state is a bedrock issue here," Rosenberg-Wohl said. FORT WORTH PRINCIPAL PICK FACES BACKLASH, INVESTIGATION OVER SOCIAL MEDIA POSTS DEFENDING SHARIA LAW The Muslim Community Association stood by its original statement, saying that the organization was "deeply concerned" over the lawsuit. "Treating students' exposure to ordinary Muslim faith and practice as inherently coercive or threatening risks reinforcing the very Islamophobia and misunderstanding that that educational engagement should help overcome," the group told Fox News Digital. Palo Alto Unified Superintendent Jason Glass informed Fox News Digital that he is reviewing the allegations but "will not comment further on pending litigation." Though some parents were upset by the field trip, some students appeared to defend the outing, suggesting that the grievances were exaggerated. Student newspaper "The Paly Voice" editor-in-chief Juni Thurston disputed claims that female students were forced to don hijabs and that students were indoctrinated with Islamic beliefs on these trips. DEARBORN SCHOOLS APOLOGIZE AFTER 200-PLUS STUDENTS MISTAKENLY SERVED PORK DURING RAMADAN "The vast majority of the people demonizing the teachers who arranged and chaperoned this field trip simply don’t know them," Thurston wrote in an op-ed for the campus newspaper. "The idea that they would be working to indoctrinate students into Islam, or any religion, is an idea extremely foreign to me as a student who has had them as my teachers for the past two years. But this narrative is nonetheless dominating media coverage of the event." However, she acknowledged concerns over Billoo's presence on the field trip and agreed that she should not have been part of the experience, though her role was "limited." In a comment to Fox News Digital, the Foundation for Individual Rights and Expression (FIRE) Vice President of Strategic Initiatives Adam Goldstein said that if students were compelled to don religious garb, this would be in violation of the First Amendment. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "Just as the First Amendment prevents public schools from forcing students to pledge allegiance to the flag, it prevents those schools from compelling them to wear religious attire. If students were required to do that as part of a curricular field trip, it would conflict with the First Amendment's bar on compelled speech," Goldstein said.
